1._: Bavli Shabbat 38a (cooking liability and disputes); Shabbat 46a (burial in sun-heated sand); Beitzah 17a (hafrashah / Yom Tov prep); Ketubot 34a (benefit from Shabbat labor); Gittin 53a (agents); Bava Kama 71a (penalties); Chullin 15a (shechitah for ill on Shabbat). Rambam Shabbat 3:4 (bishul as principal melakhah); 6:23 (general Shabbat prohibitions); 22:9 (food warmth / kelim)—these underpin Tur OC 318’s opening on bishul and liability.

3._: Bavli Shabbat 38a–39a (sun versus fire derivatives; dispute of R. Yosei and rabbis). Rambam Shabbat 9:2–3 (forbidding solar derivatives); 9:3 (springs); 22:9 (shehiyah / adjacent placement)—basis for Tur’s rules on solar heat and derivatives.

4._: Bavli Shabbat 34b–36a (insulated stew; decree lest one reheat); 45a (dry foods soaked from erev; “R. Abahu’s chicken”). Rambam Shabbat 22:8 (returning food to heat; reheating cooled dishes)—sources for reheating, gravy, and dry-food soaking.

6._: Bavli Shabbat 51a (wrapping dough). Rambam Shabbat 4:6 (kilayim-style kneading/wrapping context as cited in BY §253)—background for dough-related rulings tied to this siman.

9._: Bavli Shabbat 42a (keli rishon and spices); 42a (salt and pouring); Pesachim 41a (roast-then-boil sequence). Rambam Shabbat 22:6 (seasonings in hot pots)—sources for salt, pouring, and keli sheni/rishon rules.

11._: Bavli Shabbat 18a (vessels for washing vs. drinking). Rambam Shabbat 3:17 (hot bathing restrictions)—anchor for Tur’s bathing-vessel rulings.

12._: Bavli Shabbat 41a–42a (urn and pouring). Rambam Shabbat 12:1 (muktzeh of shards); 22:6 (pouring into kelim)—sources for kettle/urn halakhah.

13._: Bavli Shabbat 40a (lowering food for preservation). Rambam Shabbat 22:5–6 (returning food to fire; insulating)—Tur’s placement/warming rules.

14._: Bavli Shabbat 40a (insulation materials). Rambam Shabbat 22:4 (insulation decrees)—parallel to Tur’s insulation discussion.

16._: Bavli Shabbat 51a (melting fat). Rambam Shabbat 21:13 (kindling and heating)—background for fat/oil warming and “yeish bishul” concerns.

17._: Bavli Shabbat 48a (incidental heating and shehiyah)—supports Tur’s cautions about forgetting food on heat sources.
